rows.surface: Syncer verification of commit and record MACs
rows.decision: One verifier is the production path. The synchronizer reads every page and every archive through the authenticated reads in space_host.rs, which hand back a body only together with a MacVerifiedCommit. The earlier verifier, which checked an ikm and mac carried inside the commit body, and its port are deleted and nothing falls back to it: a host that answers without the response headers promotes nothing, the target fails as mac or invalid_space_mac, and the scheduler logs one line per pass counting failed targets by a fixed list of 27 reason words, never host text. The verifier, verify_commit_response in space_mac.rs, reads the Atproto-Space-Commit, Signature-Input and Signature response headers against the one-time key of its own request: exactly one member tagged atproto-space-commit that covers only that header, HMAC-SHA256 over the header re-serialized in the order received compared in constant time, then the five commit fields equal the body's commit and repo and space equal the request's. It is stricter than the pinned package on purpose: a byte sequence in any of the three headers must be the padded base64 of its bytes and no decimal may appear anywhere in them, not even in a member or parameter that a later duplicate key overwrote, because the package MACs a byte sequence's text as received and writes 1.0 as 1, while the Rust serializer writes the padded bytes and keeps 1.0; such a header is refused as invalid before the MAC, not as a MAC mismatch, so it never triggers the key refresh. It returns a MacVerifiedCommit that only space_mac.rs can make, and the authenticated reads in space_host.rs hand back a page body or an archive's records only together with one: a page's commit is the commit member of its body and an archive's is its metadata, both checked against the same three headers by this one function, an archive's before any record is kept. Only a MAC mismatch is taken for a stale KEM key: the key is refreshed once, the request is sent again with a new key share, and a second mismatch fails the target as mac. The MAC authenticates a commit and nothing else: page ops and archive records are trusted only after the store's digest check against that commit's data. Cross-checked, not run on a real host: every response case of commit-mac.json gets the pinned package's verdict, and the pinned package's response headers for the Rust request verify (stratos-produced.json).

rows.decision: The set hash, the record CID check, the operation decoder and the store functions that promote a change set or replace a whole repo state are the production path: PdsSpaceSynchronizer in pds_space_sync.rs reads the verified base, applies the ops of a poll with decode_op_page and ChangeSet::apply, proves the digest against the commit of the last page and promotes through promote_verified_space_repo, and when a rule asks for the whole repo it replaces through replace_verified_space_repo; a repo the host says does not exist is cleared through clear_verified_space_repo. SetHashState holds 1,024 little-endian 16-bit lanes; each element {collection}/{rkey}/{cid} expands through BLAKE3 extended output and is added or subtracted, and the digest is the SHA-256 of the 2,048-byte state. encode_record and record_cid give a record's canonical bytes and CID. decode_op_page and ChangeSet::apply apply typed operations to a state. promote_verified_space_repo and replace_verified_space_repo recompute the state inside one immediate transaction and compare its digest with the data of a MacVerifiedCommit; the store never takes a hash from its caller. The earlier path is deleted: SignedSpaceCommit and its verifier, the staged pages and the five stage tables (migration 11 dropped them) are gone, and nothing converts between the two verdicts. A digest mismatch is never promoted: an incremental mismatch leads to a whole-repo replacement and a mismatch on a replacement fails the target as digest. Cross-checked, not run on a real host: the pinned package's set hash vectors (lthash.json), op pages and commits (op-pages.json) and record bytes and CIDs (record-cid.json) are reproduced, and the pinned package computes the CIDs, the state and the digest that the Rust tests pin (stratos-produced.json).

rows.surface: Terminal revision of a repo catch-up
rows.decision: Promotion rests on the digest, not on a page cursor or a terminal flag: the last page of a poll is the first with no cursor, and the synchronizer promotes through promote_verified_space_repo only when the digest of the state recomputed from the base and the ops of all pages equals the data of that page's MAC-verified commit, which the store recomputes again. The base rev the caller read must still be the stored one (SpaceRepoBaseMoved is a retry next cycle). Every op's rev must be above the base rev, not above the last commit's rev and not below the op before it; a last commit below the base rev, or a stored host or generation other than the target's, is recovered by a whole-repo replacement before any rev bound is judged, because a replacement has no rev floor; the same rev with no ops is unchanged and writes nothing. replace_verified_space_repo needs no base. rows.surface: Feed pagination cursor containing a post URI
rows.decision: Opaque client state of the form {sort_at}::{uri}, taken from the last post of a full page. A malformed cursor and a well-formed stale cursor behave differently. decode splits on the first :: and accepts any two non-empty parts without checking that either is a timestamp or a URI; only a value with no :: or with an empty part decodes to None, and the feed service then serves the first page. A well-formed cursor is forwarded unchanged, and the store applies it as the predicate sort_at < cursor sort_at, or equal sort_at and uri > cursor uri; the uri part is never looked up. A cursor that names a deleted post, or a post URI in the old spelling, therefore keeps filtering: the page continues after its timestamp, and its URI decides by string order only which posts with exactly that timestamp follow. Nothing resets such a cursor to the first page. The feed generator stores no feed cursor, so its database holds nothing to migrate or invalidate for them. A cursor a client holds stays usable after the spelling change; only the tie-break among posts that share its sort_at depends on how the two spellings compare as strings. A store test pins that a cursor carrying an earlier-spelling URI is compared as an opaque string.

rows.surface: Space-form reply parent, reply root and embed record URIs in posts
rows.decision: Reply parent, reply root and embed record URIs are authoritative record content stored as submitted and never rewritten. resolveParentBoundaries accepts a parent that is a new-form space record URI, whose boundary it derives from the space DID and key without reading the parent record, or a three-part at:// URI with a DID authority, which it reads from the actor store. Any other parent, including an earlier-spelling one, a handle authority or a non-string uri, is refused as InvalidRecord before any store read, in every validate mode; before this change an earlier-spelling parent with validate false opened the service DID's actor store and answered 500. post-rules.ts recordUriCollection reads the collection of a new-form space record URI through the core parser, or of a lowercase at:// URI with exactly three parts and a non-empty collection part through AtUri, and is undefined for any other string; a space URI never reaches AtUri. Replies stay strict: isStratosUri reads only recordUriCollection, so assertReplyIsolation and PostValidator refuse a parent or root that is not a new-form space record or such a three-part at:// URI of a stratos collection. Embeds read loosely in both directions: when recordUriCollection finds nothing, they fall back to the upstream AtUri reader (any scheme case, no scheme, any depth). In a Stratos post the embed rule refuses a bsky collection through isBskyUri. In a public post, assertNoCrossNamespaceEmbed with the bsky namespace and StratosValidator.assertBskyNoCrossNamespaceEmbed refuse a stratos collection through isStratosEmbedUri. Every embed either direction refused before the respelling is still refused, except a string in the earlier spelling; a new-form space record is judged by its collection part. Nothing recognises the earlier spelling, so an earlier-spelling string is a string that is not a space URI: the upstream reader takes space for its collection, and it passes the embed guard in both directions whatever its collection part names. In a Stratos post that answer is unchanged. In a public post an earlier-spelling string naming a stratos collection was refused before and passes now. With lexicon validation on, the upstream at-uri check refuses an earlier-spelling embed in a Stratos post (more than two path segments), and with validate false it is stored as an opaque string that nothing resolves. Other answers that changed for unusual strings: a new-form space record is now classified by its collection everywhere, where the rule read no collection and PostValidator threw a parser error; and a reply parent or root naming a stratos collection in any other at:// shape (another part count, an empty collection part, another scheme case or no scheme) was accepted before and is refused now. PostValidator gives the post rule's answer for every embed and reply. Its embed check refused every string AtUri did not read as stratos, partly by letting a parser error escape; it now refuses only a bsky collection, so it passes an earlier-spelling string, a string AtUri cannot read, and any reference whose collection is in neither namespace. PostValidator is exported from stratos-core but constructed only by ValidatorFactory, which nothing outside stratos-core uses, and no service source calls assertBskyNoCrossNamespaceEmbed.
